verses.text: The word that came to Jeremiah from Yahweh, saying,
“Stand in the gate of Yahweh’s house, and proclaim there this word, and say, ‘Hear Yahweh’s word, all you of Judah, who enter in at these gates to worship Yahweh.’”
Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel says, “Amend your ways and your doings, and I will cause you to dwell in this place.
Don’t trust in lying words, saying, ‘Yahweh’s temple, Yahweh’s temple, Yahweh’s temple, are these.’
For if you thoroughly amend your ways and your doings; if you thoroughly execute justice between a man and his neighbor;
if you don’t oppress the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow, and don’t shed innocent blood in this place, neither walk after other gods to your own hurt:
then I will cause you to dwell in this place, in the land that I gave to your fathers, from of old even forever more.
Behold, you trust in lying words, that can’t profit.
Will you steal, murder, and commit adultery, and swear falsely, and burn incense to Baal, and walk after other gods that you have not known,
and come and stand before me in this house, which is called by my name, and say, ‘We are delivered;’ that you may do all these abominations?
Has this house, which is called by my name, become a den of robbers in your eyes? Behold, I, even I, have seen it,” says Yahweh.
“But go now to my place which was in Shiloh, where I caused my name to dwell at the first, and see what I did to it for the wickedness of my people Israel.
Now, because you have done all these works,” says Yahweh, “and I spoke to you, rising up early and speaking, but you didn’t hear; and I called you, but you didn’t answer:
therefore will I do to the house which is called by my name, in which you trust, and to the place which I gave to you and to your fathers, as I did to Shiloh.
I will cast you out of my sight, as I have cast out all your brothers, even the whole offspring  of Ephraim.
“Therefore don’t pray for this people, neither lift up a cry nor prayer for them, neither make intercession to me; for I will not hear you.
Don’t you see what they do in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem?

The children gather wood, and the fathers kindle the fire, and the women knead the dough, to make cakes to the queen of the sky, and to pour out drink offerings to other gods, that they may provoke me to anger.
Do they provoke me to anger? says Yahweh. “Don’t they provoke themselves, to the confusion of their own faces?”

Therefore thus says the Lord Yahweh: “Behold, my anger and my wrath shall be poured out on this place, on man, and on animal, and on the trees of the field, and on the fruit of the ground; and it shall burn, and shall not be quenched.”
Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel says: “Add your burnt offerings to your sacrifices, and eat meat.
For I didn’t speak to your fathers, nor command them in the day that I brought them out of the land of Egypt, concerning burnt offerings or sacrifices:
but this thing I commanded them, saying, ‘Listen to my voice, and I will be your God, and you shall be my people; and walk in all the way that I command you, that it may be well with you.’
But they didn’t listen nor turn their ear, but walked in their own counsels and in the stubbornness of their evil heart, and went backward, and not forward.
Since the day that your fathers came out of the land of Egypt to this day, I have sent to you all my servants the prophets, daily rising up early and sending them:
yet they didn’t listen to me, nor did they incline their ear, but made their neck stiff. They did worse than their fathers.
“You shall speak all these words to them; but they will not listen to you: you shall also call to them; but they will not answer you.
You shall tell them, ‘This is the nation that has not listened to Yahweh their God’s voice, nor received instruction. Truth has perished, and is cut off from their mouth.’
Cut off your hair, and throw it away, and take up a lamentation on the bare heights; for Yahweh has rejected and forsaken the generation of his wrath.
“For the children of Judah have done that which is evil in my sight,” says Yahweh. “They have set their abominations in the house which is called by my name, to defile it.
They have built the high places of Topheth, which is in the valley of the son of Hinnom, to burn their sons and their daughters in the fire; which I didn’t command, nor did it come into my mind.

Therefore behold, the days come”, says Yahweh, “that it shall no more be called Topheth, nor The valley of the son of Hinnom, but The valley of Slaughter; for they shall bury in Topheth, until there is no place to bury.
The dead bodies of this people shall be food for the birds of the sky, and for the animals of the earth; and no one shall frighten them away.

Then I will cause to cease from the cities of Judah, and from the streets of Jerusalem, the voice of mirth and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride; for the land shall become a waste.”

footnotes.content: The Lord's word comes precisely, named, to His servant. When God speaks, He speaks to someone, somewhere, with His full intention behind it. Here is Jeremiah—a man listening.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Stand at the gate—a public place where the crowd passes through to worship. The gate of the Lord's house is where intention meets daily life. Notice the command: proclaim *there*, not in the temple court where the elite might hear, but at the doorway, to all who enter.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Amend your ways and your doings." The Lord isn't asking for a new temple or a secret knowledge—He asks for a changed life. He promises a home for those who turn. It's so simple and so hard.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Listen to the repetition: "Yahweh's temple, Yahweh's temple, Yahweh's temple." Three times—the sound of empty words, a charm meant to protect without any change of heart. The Lord is warning: buildings and religious words are not shields.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord lays out the real amendment: execute justice between neighbors. Not an offering, not a ritual—but *justice*. The hard work of treating one another fairly, day after day. This is what the Lord wants to see in His people.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Three vulnerable groups—the foreigner, the fatherless, the widow. A nation's soul is measured by how it treats those with no power to defend themselves. And then: don't shed innocent blood, don't chase after false gods. The amendment is a whole heart turned toward the Lord and His justice.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "From of old even forever more." The promise is a home in the land forever—the same land the fathers received. Not earned, not deserved; given long ago, kept for them if they would only turn back to the Lord.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: But they do trust in lying words—words that promise safety without change, blessing without obedience. Such words profit nothing. I've seen it in my own time: the reassurance that costs us nothing is worth less than nothing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The catalog of sin: steal, murder, commit adultery, swear falsely, worship Baal, follow unknown gods. Yet they're not ashamed. How does a people come to this? One small compromise at a time, each one defended with "everyone does it."
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Then they come and stand before the Lord, speaking the magic words: "We are delivered." As if the house itself, the mere fact of entering, absolves them. Meanwhile they plan more abominations. The Lord watches this double life with steady eyes.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "A den of robbers"—a place where predators hide from justice. The house called by His name, meant to be holy, has become a shelter for wickedness. The Lord Himself says, "I have seen it." Nothing is hidden from Him, and He grieves what He sees.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Shiloh—the ancient sanctuary where the Lord's name first dwelt in the land. It stood for centuries, then the Lord abandoned it because of Israel's wickedness. The ruins are a memorial: God will not dwell with those who refuse to change.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "I spoke to you, rising up early and speaking." The image of the Lord waking while it's still dark, hurrying to call His people back. Yet they didn't hear; He called and they didn't answer. Long-suffering has a limit.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: As I did to Shiloh—a judgment that speaks across the centuries. The temple is not a talisman. The Lord will do to His own house what He did to the sanctuary of old. Trust in the building itself is false safety.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Cast out of His sight, as Ephraim was cast out—the whole northern kingdom scattered. This is the weight of the word: to be removed from the Lord's presence, to wander among nations. There is grief even in judgment.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Even the prophet is told: don't pray for them. Don't intercede. I will not hear you. A hard word—the door to repentance seems closed. Yet the Lord speaks this warning through Jeremiah, calling the people to hear before it's too late.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Don't you see what they do?" The Lord invites the prophet to observe, to witness the idolatry spread through every city and street. Ignorance is no excuse—the evidence is everywhere.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The queen of the sky—Astarte, the fertility goddess. Whole families are enlisted in worship: children gather wood, fathers kindle fire, women knead dough to make cakes. Idolatry is not a solitary sin; it draws in the household and divides hearts from the living God.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Do they provoke me to anger? Don't they provoke themselves?" The Lord turns the question inward—their rebellion wounds themselves first, brings confusion to their own faces. Sin's first victim is always the one who commits it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The anger poured out on man, animal, trees, fruit—all creation suffers the Lord's wrath when His people turn away. Judgment is total because rebellion touches everything. The fire shall burn and not be quenched.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Add your burnt offerings to your sacrifices, and eat meat." A bitter word spoken in irony—if they trust in sacrifice without obedience, take the sacrifices and eat them yourself. The ritual means nothing if the heart is turned away.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord reminds them: when I brought you out of Egypt, I didn't command burnt offerings and sacrifices. What I commanded was obedience and a listening ear. Ritual came later, but it was never the first thing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Listen to my voice, and I will be your God, and you shall be my people." The covenant is built on one word: *listen*. Walk in all the way I command, and it shall be well with you. The promise is simple, and all depends on hearing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: But they didn't listen, didn't turn their ear. They walked in their own counsels, stubbornly following their own hearts. Worse—they went backward instead of forward. The result of refusing to hear the Lord is always a backward way.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Since Egypt, the Lord has sent prophets daily, rising early to send them. Generation after generation, the Lord persisted in reaching out. His patience with His people spans centuries—yet they turned away each time.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They didn't listen, didn't incline their ear, made their neck stiff. They did worse than their fathers—each generation found new ways to rebel, adding to the old stubbornness. There is tragedy in becoming worse, not better.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: You shall speak all these words to them, but they will not listen. You shall call to them, but they will not answer. The Lord tells Jeremiah his message will fail with them—yet he must speak anyway. This is the burden of the faithful witness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A nation that has not listened to Yahweh's voice, nor received instruction. Truth has perished, cut off from their mouth. When a people stop listening to God, truth dies with them. They speak, but speak no truth.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Cut off your hair and throw it away—a sign of deep mourning and rejection. The bare heights are where lamentation is raised to heaven. The Lord has rejected and forsaken the generation of His wrath. This is the price of stubborn refusal.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The children of Judah have done evil, set their abominations in the house called by His name, defiled it. The sanctuary itself—meant to be a place of holiness—has become a monument to their unfaithfulness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The high places of Topheth in the valley of Hinnom—where they burn sons and daughters in the fire. This is child sacrifice, the deepest abomination. The Lord says: I didn't command this, it never entered my mind. Their wickedness has invented horrors beyond even what He foresaw.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The valley shall be called The Valley of Slaughter—a name that marks the place forever. So many dead that there is no room left to bury. The place of their deepest darkness becomes their grave.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The dead bodies become food for birds and animals, with no one to frighten them away. It's an image of ultimate shame—the body left unburied is the final dishonor in that world. This is what refusal brings.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo: when a people turn their backs on the Lord, joy departs—no voice of mirth, no bridegroom's song, no bride's laughter. The land becomes a waste. Yet we also know, from a longer road, that the Lord has always kept a remnant faithful, and brings healing to those who repent. The silence is not forever.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
